stories.title: St. John Properties, Somerset Companies Deliver First Phase of MD Multifamily Project
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between St. John Properties, Inc. and Somerset Companies has delivered the first phase of Melford Mansions, a luxury multifamily community within Melford Town Center in Bowie, Maryland. The initial delivery includes four five-story buildings offering 197 studios and one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences ranging from 516 to 1348 square feet. Upon final completion, Melford Mansions will feature eight buildings totaling 435 apartment homes. Melford Mansions was co-designed by Architects Collaborative and KTGY. Aumen Asner, Inc. oversaw interior design, St. John Properties’ in-house multifamily construction division completed all general contracting activities, and Bozzuto Management is the leasing and property manager. Melford Mansions represents the sixth joint venture partnership between St. John Properties and Somerset Companies. Melford Mansions is adjacent to Aspen at Melford Town Center, a 388-unit luxury multifamily community delivered by the group in 2023. The post St. John Properties, Somerset Companies Deliver First Phase of MD Multifamily Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: St. John Properties and Somerset deliver 197 units; full build-out planned at 435 units in Bowie, Maryland
Melford Mansions is sixth JV; adjacent to Aspen at Melford (388 units, 2023) creating density cluster
Bozzuto management signals institutional-grade ops; luxury positioning in Baltimore-Washington corridor
stories.summary: St. John Properties and Somerset Companies delivered the first phase of Melford Mansions in Bowie, Maryland, with 197 studio and one- to three-bedroom units; the full community will total 435 apartments across eight buildings upon completion. The property is positioned as luxury multifamily adjacent to Aspen at Melford, a 388-unit community delivered by the same partners in 2023, creating a significant residential cluster in the mixed-use Melford Town Center. Bozzuto Management handles leasing and operations, signaling institutional property management standards.
stories.impact: This represents continued densification of the Baltimore-Washington corridor's suburban submarkets (Bowie). The back-to-back delivery of 435+ units by the same developer/manager team signals confidence in demand absorption; the adjacent Aspen leasing track record will inform Melford Mansions' pricing and rent trajectory. Monitor Melford Town Center's retail/office tenancy—mixed-use success accelerates multifamily demand and justifies premium positioning.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar acquires Zonda for $800M; Zonda serves 3,000+ homebuilders, developers, lenders with lot-level construction data
Zonda 2025 revenue ~$170M; access to $400B new-home sales market; consolidates data/analytics moat
Strategic move into homebuilder software and lot inventory intelligence; signals CRE data market consolidation
stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a platform providing lot-level construction data, homebuilder software, and residential real estate marketplace services to over 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers. Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025 and operates in a $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market. The deal, announced in May, consolidates CoStar's position as a dominant provider of real estate information and analytics across residential and development sectors.
stories.impact: This is a critical signal that large CRE data and marketplace platforms are consolidating upmarket into residential development intelligence and homebuilder operations. For multifamily developers, CoStar's acquisition of lot-level and construction pipeline data on 3,000+ builders means increased transparency on land availability, development timelines, and competitive supply in target markets—raising competitive intelligence standards and potentially compressing deal sourcing windows. Expect CoStar to cross-sell development underwriting tools to multifamily players.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Arranges $20M Sale of Chicago Multifamily Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of 1515 N Fremont St., a 98-unit multifamily property with approximately 4,000 square feet of commercial space in Chicago’s Lincoln Park neighborhood. The property sold for $20.4 million.“The combination of an exceptional location, sizable scale, strong fundamentals, and limited opportunities in the market made this a very attractive investment and ultimately resulted in a successful sale,” said Kyle Stengle, senior managing director of investments in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Downtown office. Stengle represented the seller, Jack Duncan of Thesis Investment Group, and procured the buyer, Bill Silverstein of Beal Properties, a private real estate investment office.Located approximately four miles from Chicago’s Loop, 1515 N Fremont St. is situated in the heart of Lincoln Park, within walking distance of several Chicago Transit Authority stations. Nearby attractions include Oz Park, Lincoln Park, and the Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. bullets: 98-unit multifamily + 4,000 SF retail sold for $20.4M in Chicago's Lincoln Park
Limited supply and strong fundamentals cited; mixed-use ground-floor retail attractive to buyers
Marcus & Millichap brokerage activity signals institutional investor appetite for small-format, well-located Chicago assets
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the $20.4 million sale of 1515 N. Fremont Street, a 98-unit multifamily property with approximately 4,000 square feet of commercial space in Chicago's Lincoln Park neighborhood. The transaction was driven by the combination of exceptional location, sizable scale relative to neighborhood inventory, strong fundamentals, and limited opportunities in the market. Kyle Stengle of Marcus & Millichap's Chicago Downtown office represented the seller.
stories.impact: Lincoln Park is a mature, supply-constrained neighborhood; the sale of a sub-100-unit asset at $208K per unit with integral retail signals tight liquidity and buyer competition for small-format, well-located properties in Chicago's premium lakefront submarkets. This limits acquisition opportunities for new development—developers should focus on larger land assemblies or alternative neighborhoods (Pilsen, West Loop) with more available sites and lower per-unit entry costs.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions

Since 2020, the developer has been building residential projects in the coastal community near Surfside, Indian Creek and Bal Harbour. Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? Michael Troyanovsky: A really valid question, because there were other hot spot areas that a lot of people were gravitating to when we first started buying Bay Harbor. We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. We opened up a big sales office here, and we plan to stay here for the future. Who are you finding is the target demographic for your units? It’s a little bit of a mix demographic-wise, but I would say a lot of people who, whether it’s local or international, really want boutique building living. I’ve had the pleasure of meeting with all the people who purchased in the building and so many customers over the last few years, and all of them have said pretty much the same thing. bullets: Regency Development Group has four active projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida (population 6,000)
Projects include 33-unit La Maré Regency, 9-unit La Maré Signature, 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas since 2020
Developer emphasizes overlooked submarket with strong waterfront amenities and proximity to Bal Harbour, Surfside
stories.summary: Regency Development Group, a family-owned developer, has been actively building residential projects in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida, since 2020 and currently operates four active projects on the small island community. These include the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the 9-unit La Maré Signature, and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Managing partner Michael Troyanovsky highlighted the submarket's overlooked status, strong waterfront positioning, and proximity to luxury submarkets like Bal Harbour and Surfside as key drivers of development focus.
stories.impact: Bay Harbor Islands is a micro-submarket (6,000 residents) experiencing boutique residential infill by a focused developer. This signals that ultra-luxury, small-scale development (9–33 units) remains viable in affluent coastal Florida enclaves with limited supply and high barriers to entry. Competitive implications for larger multifamily developers: such markets are unlikely to support Class A garden-style or mid-rise development; focus should remain on Miami-Dade, Broward core submarkets with greater absorption capacity.

stories.title: Terreno Realty Corporation Acquires Redmond Industrial Property
stories.excerpt: Bellevue-based Terreno Realty Corporation has acquired an industrial property in Redmond, Washington, for approximately $8 million. The property consists of one industrial distribution building containing approximately 21,000 square feet on 1.5 acres. The property is located at 9680 153rd Avenue NE on Seattle’s Eastside, and provides five grade-level loading positions and parking for 56 cars. The property is vacant, and the estimated stabilized cap rate is 5.9%. The transaction follows Terreno’s April acquisition of another adjacent industrial property in Redmond for $9.3 million. That property consists of one industrial distribution building spanning approximately 33,000 square feet on 1.5 acres at 9660 153rd Avenue NE. After the existing tenant vacates, the property will be renovated to contain approximately 26,000 square feet. Terreno Realty Corporation acquires, owns and operates industrial real estate in six major coastal U.S. markets, including New York City and Northern New Jersey, Los Angeles, Miami, the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle and Washington, D.C. bullets: Terreno Realty acquires 21,000 SF industrial building in Redmond, Washington for ~$8M; 5.9% stabilized cap
Adjacent to April acquisition of 33,000 SF property ($9.3M); pre-renovation cap rate 5.9% signals tight industrial supply
Bellevue-based REIT accumulating Seattle Eastside logistics in tight leasing market
stories.summary: Terreno Realty Corporation acquired an industrial distribution property in Redmond, Washington, for approximately $8 million consisting of 21,000 square feet on 1.5 acres at 9680 153rd Avenue NE. The property is currently vacant and carries an estimated stabilized cap rate of 5.9%. This transaction follows Terreno's April acquisition of an adjacent industrial property in Redmond for $9.3 million (33,000 SF, planned renovation to 26,000 SF post-tenant exit). Terreno operates in six major coastal U.S. markets including Seattle, New York, Los Angeles, Miami, San Francisco Bay Area, and Washington, D.C.
stories.impact: Terreno's dual acquisitions of adjacent Seattle Eastside industrial assets signal strong confidence in Redmond logistics demand (proximity to tech campuses, I-405 corridor). The 5.9% stabilized cap rate reflects competitive market pricing and limited vacancy; this tightness may constrain industrial land/building availability for multifamily developers seeking conversion or adaptive-reuse opportunities in the Seattle metro. Monitor Seattle office-to-residential conversions as an offset strategy.

stories.title: Northmarq Closes Sale of $23M Multifamily Community in Spokane
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Seattle Investment Sales team, led by Tyler Smith, Steve Fischer, Joe Kinkopf and Brendan Greenheck, brokered the $22.5 million sale of Go Go Heights Apartments, a 178-unit garden-style multifamily community located at 7024 N. Colton St. in Spokane, Washington. Northmarq represented the seller, LC Gogo Heights LLC, in the transaction. The buyer was c702 LLC, a Washington-based private investment firm. ”There were a lot of market headwinds in getting this transaction to the finish line,” Kinkopf said. “The buyer was able to leverage their local team in order to execute on this deal quickly and successfully.” The transaction reflects continued investor interest in well-located multifamily assets throughout the Pacific Northwest, particularly properties that offer scale and long-term value in growing regional markets. Constructed in 1989, Go Go Heights Apartments offer residents a mix of two- and three-bedroom units featuring hardwood laminate flooring, walk-in closets, in-unit fireplaces, vaulted ceilings and private balconies. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. stories.summary: Northmarq's Seattle Investment Sales team, led by Tyler Smith, Steve Fischer, Joe Kinkopf, and Brendan Greenheck, brokered the $22.5 million sale of Go Go Heights Apartments, a 178-unit garden-style community at 7024 N. Colton Street in Spokane, Washington. The buyer was c702 LLC, a Washington-based private investment firm. The property, constructed in 1989, features two- and three-bedroom units with in-unit fireplaces, hardwood laminate flooring, and private balconies. The transaction reflects continued investor interest in well-located multifamily assets in growing regional markets across the Pacific Northwest.
stories.impact: Spokane is absorbing capital at disciplined valuations (~$126K per unit); local private investors are active acquirers of stabilized garden-style stock. For developers, this suggests limited new-development upside in Spokane—focus capital on Seattle, Portland, or Boise where rent growth and population inflow justify new construction. Spokane is a refinance/hold market, not a development play.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management acquires 25,504 SF retail condo near Miami Design District for $17.3M from Alta Developers
Miami Design District securing $125M construction loan for mixed-use expansion; Fouquet's condo/hotel in pre-sales
Ground-floor retail at Quadro condo facing train tracks; last remaining suite marketed as vacancy
stories.summary: Alta Developers sold a 25,504-square-foot retail condo on the ground floor of the Quadro mixed-use building at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard to JBL Asset Management for $17.3 million. The property faces train tracks east of the Miami Design District, an upscale 18-block open-air mall. Existing tenants include The Shade Store, a 7th Avenue furniture retailer, and Waterworks. The Miami Design District is undergoing major expansion, including a $125 million construction loan for a new mixed-use building designed by Snøhetta, and pre-sales have launched for the Fouquet's condo and hotel development by David Chipperfield.
stories.impact: Miami Design District's $125M+ capital inflow and mixed-use expansion (residential, hospitality, retail) will drive population density and daytime/evening foot traffic, benefiting nearby residential projects. For multifamily developers, this signals strong co-tenancy demand near the Design District—opportunities exist to acquire or develop residential near Biscayne Boulevard corridor ahead of Design District completion, capturing spillover renter demand from retail/hospitality employees and affluent Design District visitors.

stories.title: Williamson County Greenlights $674M Blue Origin Development Deal
stories.excerpt: Two weeks ago, Connect reported that the Williamson County economic development board had agreed to terms with Jeff Bezos’ space technology company, Blue Origin. Yesterday, the full board of commissioners approved the item, and it raises the odds that the company will build a $674 million facility in Hutto, within Williamson County. There is still one more approval required. The State of Texas needs to okay the deal. The approval would facilitate Blue Origin’s construction of approximately one million square-feet of industrial research space related to the aerospace and defense industry, located in Hutto Crossing industrial park. The facility would create as many as 2,000 jobs in 10 years. That 10-year deal includes a county abatement of 100% of real property and 50% of personal property taxes in the first five years, and 50% on real property in the last five years.  Founded in 2000, Blue Origin aims to develop reusable rocket technology to lower the cost of space travel and make it more accessible. The post Williamson County Greenlights $674M Blue Origin Development Deal appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Williamson County commissioners approve Blue Origin $674M facility deal in Hutto; State of Texas approval pending
1M SF aerospace/defense research campus; 2,000 jobs in 10 years; 100% property tax abatement first 5 years
Major employer/land use signal for Hutto Crossing industrial park; transformational for Austin metro migration demand
stories.summary: The Williamson County Board of Commissioners approved a development agreement with Blue Origin (Jeff Bezos' space technology company) for a $674 million facility in Hutto, Williamson County, Texas. The project includes approximately one million square feet of industrial research space for aerospace and defense, with projected job creation of up to 2,000 positions over 10 years. The county offered tax incentives including 100% abatement of real property and 50% abatement of personal property taxes in the first five years, with 50% real property abatement in years 6–10. State of Texas approval is still required.
stories.impact: Blue Origin's commitment to Hutto represents a major employment anchor for the Austin metro's northern corridor and will accelerate population inflow and rental demand in Williamson County submarkets (Hutto, Georgetown, Round Rock). Developers should prioritize acquisition and entitlement of multifamily land within 5–10 miles of Hutto Crossing to capture workforce housing demand ahead of 2026–2030 build-out. This is a multi-year supply window; early-stage land acquisition should command premium development intensity.

stories.title: Now Is the Time to Buy in Commercial Real Estate: Morgan Stanley
stories.excerpt: Despite a bumpy economy and increasingly high Treasury yields, one global investment firm believes now is the time to pounce on U.S. commercial real estate. Commercial Observer spoke with Tony Charles, global head of research and strategy at Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, who outlined the main takeaways from Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s mid-year 2026 real estate outlook. After a four-year recession, commercial real estate is now being repriced, giving investors a chance to acquire prime assets at low prices; supply is down across the board; and megatrends in AI, global supply chains, and aging demographics have opened up attractive entry points into infrastructure, retail and senior housing. “We certainly believe we’re entering the next up-cycle for real estate. It’s an attractive entry point,” Charles told CO in a Thursday interview. “And, given the repricing that’s now below replacement costs, we’re pretty confident in the next vintage of real estate investing.” Charles argued that the recent U.S. real estate downturn — which began in mid-2022 amid the Federal Reserve’s policy U-turn to hike interest rates coming out of COVID-19 — created “the longest downturn for real estate since the 1980s and early 1990s,” and that four years later, pricing is still down an average of 20 percent across the board. But he noted that “supply is down dramatically, so that’s obviously very helpful for real estate,” and that a strong structural macroeconomic backdrop — U.S. GDP grew 2.1 percent year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026 — has provided “a lot of green shoots that are beginning to show through.” He pointed out that CRE transaction activity increased 23 percent year-over-year in the U.S., institutional capital raising is up nearly 40 percent on the year, and that CRE debt originations are up around 20 percent year-over-year. bullets: Morgan Stanley argues CRE entering next up-cycle; assets repriced below replacement cost after 4-year downturn
Supply down across board; megatrends in AI, supply chains, aging demographics creating entry opportunities
Capital markets commentary: repricing cycle creates attractive deployment window for institutional investors
stories.summary: Tony Charles, global head of research and strategy at Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, outlined mid-2026 outlook in which U.S. commercial real estate is repricing after a four-year downturn (beginning mid-2022), creating attractive acquisition opportunities. Morgan Stanley argues that prime assets are now trading below replacement costs, supply is constrained across asset classes, and megatrends including AI, global supply chain reshoring, and aging demographics are opening attractive entry points into infrastructure, retail, and senior housing. Charles stated: "We're entering the next up-cycle for real estate. It's an attractive entry point."
stories.impact: Morgan Stanley's bullish posture signals that institutional capital is re-engaging with CRE; this will tighten cap rates, raise acquisition competition, and reduce financing availability for marginal projects. For multifamily developers, this is a near-term headwind for land and existing-asset acquisition (competition from well-capitalized funds will drive prices up) but a tailwind for construction financing (banks are loosening CRE terms). Expect faster pre-leasing requirements, tighter underwriting standards, and elevated yield expectations from equity partners.

stories.title: Whole Foods to Open Daily Shop at Murray Hill’s 509 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Whole Foods Market has leased a 9,000-square-foot retail space in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood. The 15-year deal occupies a ground-floor space and outdoor terraces at 509 Third Avenue, according to a memorandum of lease filed in city records Friday morning. The 35-story, 229-unit apartment tower, known as the Murray, was developed by Kahen Properties with Lalezarian Properties. A spokesperson for Whole Foods confirmed the lease in an email to Commercial Observer, but declined to share further details. Whole Foods’ newest Manhattan location will be on the smaller side. The store will follow the Amazon-owned grocer’s new Whole Foods Market Daily Shop format. The quick-trip urban shops sell grab-and-go meals alongside fresh produce, meat, bakery items and local specialty foods, according to the company’s website. The format was first rolled out in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024, and has since arrived in cities nationwide. Additional locations in Brooklyn and Hoboken, N.J., were announced late last year. Most recently, the grocer signed a lease for 8,121 square feet to open a daily shop at 1524 Second Avenue on the Upper East Side. Kahen Properties’ Majid Kahen signed the lease memorandum for the landlord, while Paul Hilliard, vice president of real estate at Whole Foods, signed for the grocer. It is unclear whether either party worked with an outside brokerage. The asking rent for the ground-floor space was not disclosed in the memorandum, but retail space in the nearby Herald Square area was $394 per square foot during the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. Spokespeople for Kahen and Lalezarian Properties did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Whole Foods leases 9,000 SF at 509 Third Avenue, Murray Hill, Manhattan for 15-year term
Whole Foods Daily Shop format (quick-trip, grab-and-go); ground-floor retail + outdoor terrace at 35-story mixed-use
Murray tower (229 units) developed by Kahen Properties; grocery anchor validates residential absorption in Murray Hill
stories.summary: Whole Foods Market signed a 15-year lease for 9,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space with outdoor terraces at 509 Third Avenue in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood. The location, known as the Murray, is a 35-story, 229-unit apartment tower developed by Kahen Properties with Lalezarian Properties. Whole Foods will operate the space as a Whole Foods Market Daily Shop, a smaller-format quick-trip concept selling grab-and-go meals, fresh produce, meat, bakery items, and local specialty foods. The format was first rolled out in nearby Lenox Hill in 2024.
stories.impact: Whole Foods' anchor lease at the Murray validates multifamily absorption and resident spending power in Murray Hill; it signals strong pre-leasing velocity or stabilized occupancy at the 229-unit tower. For multifamily developers, grocery-anchored ground-floor retail in residential towers improves lease-up velocity and justifies premium rents (convenience amenity). Conversely, the Daily Shop format (9,000 SF, limited assortment) suggests Whole Foods is right-sizing urban footprints; developers should plan smaller, efficient retail spaces rather than large supermarket footprints in Manhattan infill projects.
